candidates.exact_span: follow the procedures specified in the documents "Methods for Aquatic Toxicity Identification Evaluations: Phase I Toxicity Characterization Procedures" (EPA 600/6-91/003) or alternate procedures.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether Phase I toxicity characterization must follow the cited EPA method or may use unspecified alternate procedures affects which monitoring methodology requirements are applicable and whether reported TIE activities satisfy permit obligations.

candidates.exact_span: When the permittee conducts Toxicity Identification Evaluations and Confirmations, the permittee shall perform multiple identifications and follow the methods specified in the documents "Methods for Aquatic Toxicity Identification Evaluations, Phase II Toxicity Identification Procedures for Samples Exhibiting Acute and Chronic Toxicity" (EPA/600/R-92/080) and "Methods for Aquatic Toxicity Identification Evaluations, Phase III Toxicity Confirmation Procedures for Samples Exhibiting Acute and Chronic Toxicity" (EPA/600/R-92/081), as appropriate.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of when TIE/confirmation is triggered and what 'as appropriate' requires for Phase II versus Phase III methods changes which follow-up monitoring steps are obligatory after a toxicity event.

candidates.exact_span: conduct chemical specific analyses when a probable toxicant has been identified;
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a probable toxicant has been identified determines if chemical-specific monitoring is required; disagreement on that threshold changes both the applicable monitoring obligation (B) and whether absent chemical results represent a documented no-data state or missing required evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: Where the permittee has identified or suspects specific pollutant(s) and/or source(s) of effluent toxicity, the permittee shall conduct, concurrent with toxicity testing, chemical specific analyses for the identified and/or suspected pollutant(s) and/or source(s) of effluent toxicity.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The scope of 'identified or suspects' and which pollutants/sources trigger concurrent chemical analysis affects which parameters must be monitored (B), whether numeric results for those parameters should exist for limit comparison (A), and how to classify periods without such chemical data (C).

candidates.exact_span: Where toxicity was demonstrated within 24 hours of test initiation, each composite sample shall be analyzed independently. Otherwise the permittee may substitute a composite sample, comprised of equal portions of the individual composite samples, for the chemical specific analysis;
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether toxicity was demonstrated within 24 hours determines mandatory independent composite analysis versus permitted pooled composite substitution, changing sample-handling obligations (B), which reported measurements are valid for numeric limit comparison (A), and whether missing per-composite chemical data is excusable or indicates inadequate evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall initiate the TRE Action Plan within thirty (30) days of plan and schedule submittal.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The start date for the 30-day initiation clock depends on what counts as 'plan and schedule submittal'; different interpretations change whether TRE initiation was timely required during FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall submit a quarterly TRE Activities Report to the EPA WET Coordinator (6WQ-PO) in the months of January, April, July and October, containing information on toxicity reduction evaluation activities including:
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether quarterly TRE reporting was required in a given FY2025 period and what content satisfies the report obligation affects monitoring/reporting applicability (B) and what documented evidence should exist to explain missing or non-numeric TRE-related results (C).

candidates.exact_span: Any data and/or substantiating documentation which identifies the pollutant(s) and/or source(s) of effluent toxicity;
candidates.computation_change_reason: What qualifies as sufficient 'substantiating documentation' for pollutant/source identification affects whether absent numeric monitoring results can be classified as a documented no-data or conditional-not-required state versus unresolved missing evidence.
